title: Rhodes Scholarship at Oxford University
provider: The Rhodes Trust & University of Oxford
shortDescription: The world's oldest and most prestigious international graduate scholarship, enabling outstanding young leaders to study at the University of Oxford.
fullDescription:
The Rhodes Scholarship is the oldest (first awarded in 1902) and perhaps the most prestigious international scholarship programme, enabling outstanding young people from around the world to study at the University of Oxford. A Rhodes Scholarship covers Oxford University course fees, as well as providing an annual stipend. For the 2026/2027 academic year, the living stipend is £19,092 per annum (£1,591 per month) from which Scholars pay all living expenses, including accommodation.

The selection process seeks young people of outstanding intellect, character, leadership, and commitment to service. Rhodes Scholars are people who have a vision of how the world could be better and the energy to make that vision a reality.
eligibility: Completed an undergraduate degree with First Class Honours or GPA above 3.7/4.0
Aged between 18 and 24 at the time of application
Demonstrated moral force of character and instincts to lead
High proficiency in written and spoken English
Citizens of all eligible Rhodes constituencies across 60+ countries
benefits: 100% full university and college tuition fees covered
Annual living stipend of £19,092 paid monthly
Two economy class flights (at start and end of studies)
Tier 4 student visa application fee and International Health Surcharge covered
Access to the Rhodes Leadership Development Programme and global alumni network
requirements: Official academic transcripts and degree certificates
Comprehensive Curriculum Vitae (CV) / Resume
Statement of Purpose / Academic Study Plan (up to 1,000 words)
Personal statement detailing values, leadership, and public service (750 words)
Six letters of recommendation (minimum 4 academic, 2 character/leadership)
Valid passport and proof of age / citizenship

title: Google Software Engineering Summer Internship 2027
shortDescription: Join Google engineers working on scalable distributed systems, search algorithms, machine learning models, and cloud technologies.
fullDescription:
Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. As a Software Engineering Intern, you will work on our core products and services like Google Search, YouTube, Android, Cloud, or Gemini AI.

You will be paired with a dedicated mentor and host engineer who will guide you throughout your 12-14 week internship, helping you design, implement, and ship production code.
eligibility: Currently enrolled in an Associate, Bachelor's, or Master's program in Computer Science or related STEM field
Experience coding in C++, Java, Python, Go, or Rust
Solid foundation in Data Structures, Algorithms, and Software Design
Expected graduation date between December 2026 and August 2028
Authorization to work in the USA or eligible for J-1 intern visa sponsorship
benefits: Competitive monthly stipend of $8,800 - $9,500 based on location
Furnished corporate housing or generous monthly housing stipend ($2,500/mo)
Round-trip airfare and ground transport covered
Free gourmet meals, micro-kitchens, and wellness campus facilities
Direct conversion opportunity to Full-Time Software Engineer after graduation
requirements: Updated Resume highlighting coding projects, GitHub, and internships
Current unofficial academic transcript
Technical assessment completion via Google online coding platform
Two virtual 45-minute technical interviews focusing on problem solving and algorithms

title: DAAD Helmut-Schmidt Master's Scholarship in Germany
awardAmount: €934 / Month + Full Tuition + German Language Course
shortDescription: Supports future leaders from developing countries who wish to promote democracy, public policy, and social justice in their home regions.
fullDescription:
The DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme (known as Public Policy and Good Governance) offers future leaders from developing and emerging countries the chance to acquire a Master's degree in disciplines that are of particular relevance for the social, political, and economic development of their home countries.

Courses are taught in English and German at renowned German universities including Hertie School of Governance, University of Erfurt, and University of Passau.
eligibility: Undergraduate degree in Political Science, Economics, Law, Public Administration, or related field
Graduated with above average academic marks (top 30% of class)
Undergraduate degree must have been obtained within the last 6 years
Demonstrated commitment to civic engagement and public interest
Proficient in English (minimum TOEFL iBT 80 or IELTS 6.5)
benefits: Tuition-free Master's program at selected partner universities in Germany
Monthly scholarship rate of €934 per month
Contributions to health, accident, and personal liability insurance in Germany
Travel allowance for flights to and from Germany
Study and research grant of €460 per year plus free 6-month intensive German course
requirements: DAAD application form filled and signed
Hand-signed Curriculum Vitae (Europass format)
Letter of Motivation (maximum 2 pages) detailing why this program fits your career goals
University diplomas and official transcripts with certified German/English translations
Two letters of recommendation from university professors or employers

title: Microsoft Research AI & Robotics Fellowship 2027
shortDescription: A two-year global fellowship recognizing top PhD candidates conducting pioneering research in artificial intelligence, robotics, and quantum computing.
fullDescription:
The Microsoft Research PhD Fellowship is a global program that identifies and empowers promising doctoral students in computer science, robotics, and applied mathematics. The fellowship covers 100% of tuition and fees for two consecutive academic years, along with a $42,000 USD annual living stipend.

Recipients receive an invitation to attend the annual Microsoft Research PhD Summit, dedicated cloud compute allocation on Azure, and direct mentoring from world-renowned scientists at Microsoft Research laboratories.

Focusing on Machine Learning, Autonomous Robotics, Computer Vision, or NLP
Completed at least one year of doctoral studies by the application date
Strong track record of publications in top tier conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, IROS, etc.)
Nominated by their university department chair or faculty advisor

$42,000 annual living stipend

Direct technical mentorship with principal researchers

Three letters of recommendation from academic advisors and research collaborators

title: Tesla Autopilot & Battery Systems Engineering Internship
shortDescription: Hands-on engineering internship working on high-voltage battery architecture, neural network inference, and full self-driving hardware.
fullDescription:
At Tesla, our interns tackle real-world engineering problems from day one. You won't be observing; you will be writing firmware, building simulations, designing mechanical battery packs, and debugging autonomous vehicle telematics.

You will collaborate with world-class engineers who are accelerating the world's transition to sustainable energy.
eligibility: Enrolled in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Mechatronics
Demonstrated hands-on experience through Formula SAE, Solar Car, robotics clubs, or independent hardware projects
Proficient in C, C++, Python, MATLAB/Simulink, or CAD (SolidWorks/CATIA)
Ability to thrive in an agile, fast-paced, high-intensity environment
benefits: $45 per hour compensation with overtime pay eligibility
Full relocation travel package and corporate housing assistance
Tesla vehicle employee discount and complimentary Supercharging access
Mentorship from leading battery and autonomous driving system engineers
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance during internship
requirements: Engineering portfolio or GitHub repo showcasing personal projects
Resume including detailed bullet points on hardware/software projects
Most recent academic transcript
Available for a minimum 12-16 week full-time commitment

title: Chevening Scholarship for Master's Study in the UK
shortDescription: The UK government’s global scholarship programme, funded by the FCDO, awarding future leaders full funding to study any master's degree in the UK.
fullDescription:
Chevening is the UK Government’s global scholarship programme that offers future leaders the unique opportunity to study in the UK. These scholarships are awarded to outstanding professionals from all over the world to pursue a one-year master’s degree in any subject at any UK university.

Chevening provides fully-funded scholarships, leaving you free to focus on achieving your academic goals and enjoying the experience of a lifetime. You will live and study in the UK for a year, during which you will develop professionally and academically, grow your network, and experience UK culture.
eligibility: Citizen of a Chevening-eligible country or territory
Return to your country of citizenship for a minimum of two years after your award has ended
Completed an undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a master's program in the UK (typically 2:1 honours)
Minimum of two years (equivalent to 2,800 hours) of demonstrable work experience
Apply to three different eligible UK university courses and receive an unconditional offer from at least one
benefits: 100% full payment of university tuition fees
Monthly living allowance / stipend tailored to city of study
Economy class travel to and from the UK
Arrival and departure allowances
Cost of one visa application and travel grant to attend Chevening events in the UK
requirements: Online Chevening application including four 500-word essay answers on Leadership, Networking, Studying in the UK, and Career Plans
Certified copies of university degree certificates and transcripts
Two references from professional or academic supervisors
Unconditional offer letter from at least one eligible UK university

title: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Banking Summer Analyst
shortDescription: A 10-week summer program for students interested in mergers and acquisitions, financial restructuring, and capital markets advisory.
fullDescription:
The Goldman Sachs Summer Analyst Internship is an intensive 10-week program designed to introduce undergraduate and master's students to the financial services industry. You will be fully immersed in real deal teams, building financial models, preparing client pitches, and analyzing M&A transactions for Fortune 500 companies.

Top performers will receive an offer for a full-time Analyst role upon completion of their degree.
eligibility: Penultimate year student graduating in late 2027 or summer 2028
All majors welcome; Economics, Finance, Mathematics, and Engineering preferred
Strong analytical, quantitative, and interpersonal communication skills
High proficiency in financial modeling and Microsoft Excel is an asset
Demonstrated track record of leadership and academic excellence
benefits: Highly competitive salary ($110,000 annualized base pro-rated over 10 weeks)
$2,500 housing stipend for interns relocating to New York or London
Comprehensive 1-week training program covering Wall Street financial valuation
Direct exposure to Managing Directors and senior executive leadership
High conversion rate to full-time Investment Banking Analyst roles
requirements: One-page resume conforming to standard Wall Street formatting
Cover letter expressing interest in specific division (M&A, Leveraged Finance, Tech Banking)
Completion of HireVue digital video assessment upon submission
Superday final round interviews (behavioral and technical finance questions)

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees (EMJMD) in Europe
awardAmount: €1,400 / Month + Complete Tuition across 3 EU Countries
shortDescription: Study across at least two European countries and graduate with a joint or double master's degree funded completely by the EU.
fullDescription:
Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are high-level integrated study programmes at master level. They are designed and delivered by an international partnership of higher education institutions from different countries worldwide.

The EU-funded scholarship covers the cost of a student's participation in the programme, travel, and a living allowance of €1,400 per month for the full duration of 24 months. You will spend semesters at universities in different European capitals, gaining a truly international academic perspective.
eligibility: Completed a first higher education degree (Bachelor's or equivalent 180 ECTS)
Outstanding academic transcripts in relevant scientific or quantitative discipline
Fluency in English (IELTS 6.5 or equivalent TOEFL)
Open to students from all nationalities worldwide (Program and Partner countries)
Ready to relocate between different European universities every semester
benefits: 100% tuition, laboratory fees, and library charges paid directly to universities
Monthly living allowance of €1,400 per month for up to 24 months (€33,600 total)
Comprehensive worldwide medical and travel insurance
Full travel allowance (€3,000 per year) and installation grant (€1,000)
Joint Master Degree accredited in multiple EU member states
requirements: Detailed CV listing academic background and research experience
Certified copy of Bachelor's degree certificate and transcript of records
Motivation letter explaining chosen master's track and study plan
Two academic reference letters from university professors
Valid passport copy

title: WHO Global Health & Epidemic Prevention Fellowship
shortDescription: A specialized 12-month fellowship for medical and public health researchers dedicated to infectious disease surveillance and global health diplomacy.
fullDescription:
The World Health Organization Global Health Fellowship provides early-career medical doctors, epidemiologists, and public health scholars with deep immersion into international public health response mechanisms.

Fellows are stationed at the WHO Headquarters in Geneva or regional offices, working side by side with technical experts on pandemic preparedness, maternal health, and vaccine equity.
eligibility: Graduated with an MD, MBBS, Master in Public Health (MPH), or related medical degree
At least 2 years of relevant clinical or epidemiological research experience
Fluency in English or French; working knowledge of another UN language is a plus
Demonstrated commitment to underserved communities and healthcare equity
benefits: $3,000 monthly living stipend for 12 months
All official travel expenses to international field missions covered
UN health and emergency repatriation insurance
Mentorship from WHO technical officers and senior epidemiologists
Publication support in WHO bulletin and peer-reviewed medical journals
requirements: Medical / Public Health credentials and licensing documentation
Comprehensive CV outlining field experience and research papers
Statement of Intent focused on infectious disease or global health equity
Three professional letters of recommendation from medical faculty or health authorities

You will learn to evaluate technical requirements, recommend architectural best practices, and build prototype solutions using serverless, containers, database engines, and AI services.

This position provides full remote flexibility with optional in-person hub collaboration.

Basic understanding of computer networking, operating systems, and web protocols
Familiarity with at least one programming language (Python, Node.js, Java, or Go)
Passionate about cloud architecture, DevOps, and customer-facing problem solving
benefits: $8,500 monthly stipend with full remote work stipend for home office setup
100% voucher coverage for AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner & Solutions Architect exams
Direct 1-on-1 mentorship from Senior Principal AWS Architects
Internal access to Amazon executive speaker series and technical workshops
Seamless return offer pipeline for full-time Solutions Architect positions
requirements: Resume demonstrating technical coursework, projects, or cloud certifications
GitHub portfolio or live deployed project links
Completion of online technical assessment
Behavioral and architectural interview based on Amazon Leadership Principles

shortDescription: An intensive summer fellowship bringing emerging student leaders to Harvard to study international development, economic policy, and governance.
fullDescription:
The Harvard Kennedy School Public Policy Summer Fellowship offers selected undergraduate scholars the opportunity to immerse themselves in policy analysis, quantitative evaluation, and leadership training on the Harvard campus.

Scholars attend seminars by Harvard professors, former heads of state, and global diplomats while conducting an independent capstone policy memo.
eligibility: Rising juniors or seniors enrolled in an undergraduate program worldwide
Commitment to public service, government, NGO work, or social impact
GPA equivalent to 3.5 or above
All academic majors are welcome (Economics, Political Science, Sociology, History, STEM)
benefits: $12,000 non-taxable fellowship grant
Complimentary accommodation in Harvard Yard residential houses
Meal plan and dining hall access across Harvard University
Unlimited access to Harvard University libraries and research archives
Certificate of Completion issued by Harvard Kennedy School
requirements: Academic transcript of all completed university semesters
Two letters of recommendation from faculty members
Policy interest statement (500 words) addressing a major global challenge
Resume detailing campus leadership and community service

Our consultants come from diverse academic backgrounds ranging from humanities to engineering.

Senior Partner mentorship and career coaching
Direct conversion to full-time Business Analyst with graduate school tuition support
